clinical_events.description: Patient reports dry cough for about ten days.
Lisinopril prescribed; intended start February 13, ingestion not observed.
Chest radiograph report finalized with right basal opacity.
Repeat chest radiograph due April 30; patient informed.
Consultation records cough onset as May 26, with possible medication or reflux contribution.
Lisinopril discontinued; losartan prescribed from July 9.
CT chest booked for July 29; no completed CT or spirometry result in supplied record.

documents.title: Primary care assessment
documents.author: Dr Mira Vale (fictional)
documents.text_content:
SYNTHETIC — NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Chief concern: Dry cough and intermittent heartburn.
History: Cough present for about ten days, mainly evenings; no fever, hemoptysis or breathlessness. Never smoked. No previous lung disease. No regular medication and no previous ACE inhibitor use reported. Works at a fictional stationery office; no dust exposure reported. No known drug allergies reported.
Examination: Temperature 36.7 C, pulse 76/min, BP 148/92 mmHg, oxygen saturation 98% on air. Chest clear. Weight 82.0 kg.
Assessment: Recent cough with symptomatic reflux; post-viral cough also possible. Elevated office BP requires repeat assessment.
Plan: Four-week omeprazole trial for heartburn; review persistent cough and repeat BP. Return earlier for breathlessness, blood in sputum or systemic symptoms.

documents.title: Blood pressure and symptom review
documents.author: Dr Mira Vale (fictional)
documents.text_content:
SYNTHETIC — NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Interval history: Heartburn improved after the four-week course. Dry cough continues intermittently and has not fully settled. No dyspnea at rest, hemoptysis or fever.
Examination: BP 152/94 mmHg after rest, pulse 78/min, oxygen saturation 98% on air. Weight 81.5 kg. Chest clear.
Assessment: Repeated hypertension; cough of uncertain cause.
Plan: Lisinopril 5 mg once daily prescribed, first intended dose tomorrow. Discuss possible cough as an adverse effect. Renal function and potassium sampled today; repeat at next visit. Chest radiograph requested if cough persists. Medication order is not confirmation of ingestion.

documents.title: Persistent cough review
documents.author: Dr Mira Vale (fictional)
documents.text_content:
SYNTHETIC — NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
History: Reports taking lisinopril since February 13. Cough persists, with occasional scant clear sputum. Heartburn remains better. No fever or hemoptysis.
Findings: BP 138/86 mmHg, saturation 97% on air, weight 80.8 kg. Faint right basal crackles, no wheeze.
Assessment: Persistent cough; chest radiograph and blood tests obtained today.
Plan: Review finalized results; radiograph follow-up will be arranged according to report. Renal function monitoring after starting lisinopril. Return for worsening symptoms.

documents.title: Follow-up consultation
documents.author: Dr Mira Vale (fictional)
documents.text_content:
SYNTHETIC — NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
History: Cough remains daily; has reduced exercise tolerance on stairs. No fever or hemoptysis. Reports regular lisinopril use.
Examination: BP 136/84 mmHg, saturation 97% on air, weight 79.5 kg; right basal crackles remain subtle.
Assessment: Persistent respiratory symptoms. Repeat chest radiograph obtained today.
Plan: Await radiology comparison. Internal medicine review requested. Patient advised to seek urgent review for breathlessness at rest or hemoptysis.

documents.title: Internal medicine consultation
documents.author: Dr Leon Ash (fictional)
documents.text_content:
SYNTHETIC — NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Reason for review: Cough, intermittent reflux and worry about work.
History: Cough first began on May 26, 2026; no cough before then. Taking lisinopril 5 mg daily since February. Reports occasional heartburn and poor sleep when anxious. Denies fever and hemoptysis.
Exam: BP 132/82 mmHg, saturation 97% on air, weight 78.8 kg. No wheeze.
Working impression: ACE inhibitor-associated cough is possible; reflux and anxiety may amplify symptoms. Previous radiology documents are not attached to this consultation packet.
Plan: Short symptom diary, trial reflux treatment for recurrent heartburn, arrange medication review and obtain prior imaging reports. No definitive etiology established.
Prescription MED-001-04: Omeprazole 20 mg orally once daily from June 5 through July 2, ordered today at 09:40 +03:00 for recurrent heartburn.

documents.title: Urgent ambulatory assessment
documents.author: Dr Nia Reed (fictional)
documents.text_content:
SYNTHETIC — NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Presentation: Increasing cough, fatigue and breathlessness walking uphill. No breathlessness at rest, hemoptysis or fever. Reports ongoing lisinopril use through this morning.
Exam: Temperature 37.0 C, pulse 92/min, BP 130/80 mmHg, oxygen saturation 95% on air, weight 77.0 kg. Right basal crackles without wheeze.
Results: Blood tests and chest radiograph obtained; see linked reports.
Assessment: Persistent cough with weight loss and unresolved radiographic abnormality requires expedited respiratory assessment. ACE inhibitor contribution remains possible.
Plan: Stop lisinopril today; prescribe losartan for BP. Urgent respiratory referral and CT chest requested. Stable for ambulatory follow-up after assessment; explicit return precautions given. No final diagnosis assigned.

documents.title: Respiratory consultation
documents.author: Dr Ivo Fern (fictional)
documents.text_content:
SYNTHETIC — NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
History: Persistent cough and reduced exercise tolerance. Patient reports stopping lisinopril on July 8 and taking losartan thereafter. Cough has not clearly changed over the subsequent two weeks. Reflux symptoms improved with treatment. No hemoptysis.
Exam: BP 132/84 mmHg, saturation 96% on air, weight 77.2 kg; persistent right basal crackles.
Assessment: Etiology remains unresolved. Focal radiographic opacity and inflammatory-marker trend need further characterization. A short interval after stopping an ACE inhibitor does not settle its contribution. Anxiety may coexist and does not explain the imaging finding by itself.
Plan: CT chest booked for July 29; no completed CT result is available in this record. Spirometry requested; no result yet. Review after imaging; urgent return for worsening breathlessness, chest pain or hemoptysis.

documents.author: Dr Mira Vale (fictional)
documents.text_content:

documents.title: Ambulatory follow-up instructions
documents.author: Dr Nia Reed (fictional)
documents.text_content:
SYNTHETIC — NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Ambulatory disposition following urgent assessment. Stop lisinopril; losartan 25 mg once daily prescribed from tomorrow. Do not take both medicines together. Respiratory review booked July 22. CT requested, appointment pending. Seek urgent care for breathlessness at rest, hemoptysis, chest pain or rapid deterioration. No CT or spirometry result available today.

documents.title: Medication reconciliation
documents.author: Dr Ivo Fern (fictional)
documents.text_content:
SYNTHETIC — NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Patient reports no lisinopril since July 8 and reports taking losartan 25 mg each morning since July 9. No dispensing or administration record supplied. Omeprazole course for recurrent heartburn completed July 2; symptoms improved. No clear cough improvement yet. This is patient-reported use, not observed administration.

documents.author: Dr Sera Flint, radiology (fictional)
documents.text_content:
SYNTHETIC — NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
Exam: PA and lateral chest radiograph.
Indication: Persistent cough.
Technique: Standard two-view study (fictional report).
Comparison: None available. Findings: Small ill-defined right lower-zone air-space opacity. No pleural effusion. Cardiomediastinal silhouette not enlarged. Impression: Nonspecific right basal opacity; inflammatory change or subsegmental atelectatic change are considerations. Repeat chest radiograph in six weeks to assess resolution.
